titleEn: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver & Metro Vancouver: 2026 Costs, Risks & What Homeowners Need to Know
titleZh: 溫哥華及大溫地區聚丁烯（Poly-B）管道更換完整指南（2026年版）
contentEn:
Vancouver-area homeowners with homes built between 1986 and 1997 face a hidden threat: Poly-B piping. Grey in colour with dull fitting connections, polybutylene (Poly-B) was installed in an estimated 60,000 Metro Vancouver homes before being discontinued due to failure rates linked to chlorine reactions in municipal water supplies.

How to Identify Poly-B Pipes in Your Home

Poly-B pipes are grey plastic tubing 12–25 mm in diameter with dull white or grey crimp or insert fittings. They typically run through basements, crawlspaces, and inside walls. A plumber can confirm within 30 minutes at no charge as part of an inspection. Look for: grey plastic pipes running to water heaters, faucets, and fixture supply lines; visible pipes in unfinished basements or mechanical rooms; and any pipes installed during the 1986–1997 construction boom.

What Happens When Poly-B Fails

Poly-B fails in two ways: slow micro-fracture leaks that cause hidden water damage over months, and sudden burst failures that can release thousands of litres of water in minutes. BC insurers have classified Poly-B as high-risk since the early 2000s; many refuse to insure affected homes at all, and those that do charge significantly higher premiums. A single water-loss insurance claim from a Poly-B burst pipe can exceed $75,000 in structural remediation, flooring replacement, and mould remediation.

2026 Poly-B Replacement Cost in Vancouver and Metro Vancouver

Re-plumbing an average Vancouver single-family home with copper or PEX-A pipe costs $8,000–$18,000 depending on the number of fixtures and layout complexity. Re-piping a townhouse or condo runs $4,000–$9,000. Surrey, Richmond, and Coquitlam homes fall within these ranges. PEX-A is now the standard replacement material — flexible, freeze-resistant, and backed by 25-year manufacturer warranties. Reno Stars provides a written 25-year labour warranty on all re-piping work.

Does Home Insurance Cover Poly-B Replacement?

Most mainstream BC insurers no longer cover homes with documented Poly-B piping. Some specialty insurers offer coverage with a mandatory inspection contingency. Proactive replacement eliminates the insurance risk entirely and can reduce monthly premiums by $50–$150/month. Reno Stars provides a full Poly-B assessment as a free service to help homeowners understand their exposure before committing to replacement.

Why Choose Full Re-piping Over Patch Repairs

Every patch repair leaves other weak sections of pipe in place. A visible leak at one fitting means the same material throughout your system is under the same stress. Full re-piping with a 25-year labour warranty eliminates recurrence risk and is typically required before an insurer will provide coverage on an affected property. Reno Stars has completed over 40 Poly-B re-piping projects across Metro Vancouver since 2022.

Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver: Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if my home has Poly-B pipes?

Poly-B pipes are grey plastic tubing 12–25 mm in diameter, typically found in basements, crawlspaces, and running to water fixtures. They have dull grey or white fittings rather than shiny copper ones. A licensed plumber can confirm within 30 minutes. Reno Stars offers free Poly-B inspections.

Is Poly-B pipe covered by insurance in BC?

Most mainstream BC insurers will not issue new policies on homes with documented Poly-B. Some specialty insurers provide coverage with inspection requirements. Proactive replacement is the only way to restore access to standard home insurance coverage.

How long does Poly-B replacement take?

A full re-pipe for a single-family home typically takes 3–5 days. The water supply is shut off only during active work; Reno Stars coordinates to restore water each evening. A townhouse or condo re-pipe is usually completed in 1–2 days.

What is the cost of Poly-B pipe replacement in Vancouver 2026?

Re-plumbing a Vancouver single-family home costs $8,000–$18,000 depending on fixtures and layout. Townhouses and condos run $4,000–$9,000. Prices include all labour, materials, permit fees, and wall patching.

Should I replace Poly-B before selling my Vancouver home?

Yes. Poly-B disclosure is mandatory in BC real estate transactions, and most buyers either demand a price reduction or require full replacement before completing the purchase. Proactive replacement at $8,000–$18,000 protects the sale and eliminates post-closing insurance complications.

contentZh:
1986年至1997年間建造的溫哥華地區住宅，普遍面臨一種隱藏威脅：聚丁烯（Poly-B）管道。這種灰色塑膠管道當時安裝於估計60,000戶大溫哥華家庭，因與自來水含氯反應導致故障率過高而被停用。

如何識別家中的Poly-B管道

Poly-B管道為直徑12至25毫米的灰色塑膠管，帶有啞光白色或灰色壓接或插入式管件。通常分佈於地下室、爬行空間和牆內。水管工可在30分鐘內確認是否為Poly-B。識別標誌：通往熱水器的灰色塑膠管道；未裝修地下室可見的管道；以及1986至1997年間建造房屋內的所有管道。

Poly-B管道故障的後果

Poly-B以兩種方式故障：緩慢的微裂紋滲漏（數月內造成隱性水損害），以及突然爆裂（數分鐘內釋放數千升水）。BC省保險公司自2000年代初已將Poly-B列為高風險；許多保險公司拒絕為受影響房屋承保，另一些則收取巨額保費。單次Poly-B爆裂漏水保險理賠，結構修復、地板更換和黴菌處理的費用可超過$75,000。

2026年溫哥華及大溫地區Poly-B更換費用

用銅管或PEX-A管道更換溫哥華典型獨立住宅的管道，費用為$8,000至$18,000，具體取決於固定裝置數量和佈局複雜程度。鎮屋或公寓的管道更換費用為$4,000至$9,000。高貴林、列治文和素里的房屋費用在此範圍內。PEX-A是現時標準更換材料——柔韌、抗凍，並有製造商25年質保。聚星裝修對所有管道更換工程提供書面25年人工質保。

房屋保險是否涵蓋Poly-B更換？

大多數主流BC保險公司不再承保有Poly-B管道記錄的房屋。部分專業保險公司提供帶檢查條件的承保。主動更換可完全消除保險風險，並可將每月保費降低$50至$150。聚星裝修提供免費Poly-B評估，幫助業主在決定更換前了解風險程度。

為什麼選擇全面管道更換而非局部修補

每次局部修補都會將其他薄弱管道段留在原位。一處可見的滲漏意味著整個系統中相同材質的管道都承受相同壓力。全面管道更換配合25年人工質保，可消除復發風險，也是受影響房屋獲得保險覆蓋的通常前提。聚星裝修自2022年以來，已在整個大溫哥華地區完成超過40個Poly-B管道更換項目。

溫哥華Poly-B管道更換常見問題

如何判斷我的房屋是否有Poly-B管道？

Poly-B管道為直徑12至25毫米的灰色塑膠管，通常見於地下室、爬行空間和通往用水裝置的管道，帶有啞光灰色或白色管件而非閃亮銅件。持牌水管工可在30分鐘內確認。聚星裝修提供免費Poly-B檢查。

BC省的Poly-B管道有保險覆蓋嗎？

大多數主流BC保險公司不會為有Poly-B管道記錄的房屋承保。部分專業保險公司提供帶檢查條件的承保。主動更換是恢復標準房屋保險覆蓋的唯一途徑。

Poly-B更換需要多長時間？

獨立住宅的全面管道更換通常需要3至5天。供水只在 active施工期間中斷；聚星裝修會協調每晚恢復供水。鎮屋或公寓的管道更換通常1至2天完成。

2026年溫哥華Poly-B管道更換的費用是多少？

溫哥華獨立住宅的管道更換費用為$8,000至$18,000，具體取決於固定裝置和佈局。鎮屋和公寓費用為$4,000至$9,000。價格包含所有人工、材料、許可證費用和牆面修補。

出售溫哥華房屋前應該更換Poly-B管道嗎？

應該。BC省房地產交易中，Poly-B披露是強制性的，大多數買家要么要求價格折讓，要么要求在完成交易前进行全面更換。主動更換費用$8,000至$18,000，可保護交易並消除售後保險問題。
